name: emergency_watchdog

installed-executable.rationale: Native scheduler definitions name this user-owned executable. The owner qualifies a staged image and durably publishes it; arbitrary relocation would break those definitions.

previous-executable.rationale: One checksum-bound prior executable, replaced only by the serialized update owner before its next publication. It must survive an interrupted or failed publication.

publication-receipt.rationale: Schema is owned by emergency-watchdog/update.go. The single bounded receipt carries publication/restoration intent and failed-image suppression; native recovery may consume it without source access.

publication-lock.rationale: Empty cross-process lock inode shared by setup and native recovery; unlinking an active lock would permit competing writers.

storage.rationale: The existing user-scoped native executable namespace holds a bounded current/prior pair and one local-schema receipt. These pinned native artifacts are not scenario storage-class roots. The owner bounds executable reads and prunes only its abandoned regular staging files under the shared lock.

description: Install the portable emergency watchdog and its native user scheduler entry so setup owns the last line of defense instead of a hand-placed unit

setpoint_path.description: Optional path to the shared reliability setpoint. Pressure and sustain bars are read from this contract by the installed watchdog binary.

notes: The watchdog's pressure thresholds are declared in infrastructure-manager/setpoint/reliability-setpoint.json; this manifest intentionally carries no private CPU deadband. The portable report-only decision binary reads hostpressure directly. Platform scheduling remains owned by each host's native scheduler.
